mainText:
National's drug testing plan for jobseekers leads today, as the election campaign and a Christchurch missing person case dominate the news.

New Zealand.

National has announced a five point plan for beneficiaries, including random drug testing for people on Jobseeker Support and cuts to the benefit from 2028. Christopher Luxon says drug testing MPs is not party policy. Labour has yet to respond in detail. The policy follows National's costings clash with Labour earlier this week over Investment Boost numbers.

Police say their inquiries suggest missing Christchurch father Braydon Hepworth, 21, missing since September, is no longer alive. Multiple search warrants have been executed across Christchurch, including a scene examination at his last known address, now completed. Police say people in the community know what happened to him.

One person has died in a house fire at Wharekaho, near Whitianga, in the Coromandel, called in around two twenty a.m. A second occupant raised the alarm and escaped without injury. Fire and police investigators are examining the scene.

RNZ's chief financial officer Hilary Parker has resigned unexpectedly, with board member Richard Dellabarca stepping in as the broadcaster prepares its annual accounts. RNZ says it still expects to meet its reporting deadline, with further cost cuts expected.

Petrol prices have hit new highs this week, and financial mentors say motorists are increasingly putting fuel purchases on buy now pay later schemes such as Afterpay, warning it risks a debt cycle for households already squeezed by rates and weather costs.

In the Bay of Plenty, Dallas Hohua, who stabbed a friend to death after a party, has had his manslaughter sentence reduced and may serve as little as two years. The Western Bay of Plenty byelection process continues following councillor Alan Kurtovich's resignation over the council's Māori wards decision, which he says was absolutely the right call despite the cost of the vote.

World.

Rwanda backed rebels have entered Goma in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with residents reporting gunfire and shelling after Congolese troops were overrun. The United Nations estimates more than one million displaced people are now inside the city.

Israel has marked three years since the October the seventh Hamas attack, with memorial events held nationwide. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has refused to take personal responsibility or order a state inquiry into the failures that day, and families of victims are demanding accountability.

Russia launched an overnight barrage of one hundred and thirty drones and forty eight cruise and ballistic missiles at Ukraine, killing at least twenty four people. Five children were among nineteen killed when a missile destroyed thirty flats in a residential block in the country's north while families slept.

Kenya has quarantined ten people linked to the country's first confirmed Ebola case, after the patient travelled through multiple cities in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda before flying into Kenya. Screening gaps at borders are under scrutiny.

Technology.

The Pentagon has stopped using Anthropic's AI tools after blacklisting the company in February as a supply chain risk, when Anthropic refused to strip safety guardrails from its systems. OpenAI has fired staff for what it called mishandling sensitive information, after they were investigated for sharing data with an outside AI evaluation group. Separately, OpenAI says teenage use of ChatGPT is limited, but independent research cited by the BBC found guardrails meant to protect teenage users often failed, calling the current risk unacceptable.

Sport.

Rugby. The All Blacks face the Wallabies in the Bledisloe Cup at Eden Park on Saturday. Scott Barrett could start on his comeback, with brother Beauden also in line for a significant role. Richie Mo'unga and Fehi Fineanganofo are ruled out, Fineanganofo with concussion and a hamstring strain from the Bay of Plenty match. Wallabies flanker Fraser McReight, winning his forty seventh cap, credits former coach Dave Rennie, now his opponent, with tough love early in his career.

League. Kalyn Ponga will make his Kiwis debut and Stacey Waaka becomes a dual international, both named in New Zealand's Rugby League World Cup squads. Jacob Laban has chosen to represent the Kiwis over his birthplace, saying he got his father's blessing first.

Cricket. India has recalled seamer Bhuvneshwar Kumar for the Twenty20 series against the Black Caps, his first call up in four years, on the back of a strong Indian Premier League season. Former Black Cap BJ Watling joins the national side as batting coach from November the sixteenth, completing a transition from incumbent Luke Ronchi.

Golf. Jon Rahm is leaving LIV Golf, telling a bankruptcy court hearing the terms for a revamped LIV 2.0 are unacceptable. The two time major champion's exit deepens doubts over the circuit's Saudi backed future.

Tennis. American Brandon Nakashima has signed up for January's ASB Classic in Auckland, the second top twenty player to commit after last year's champion Jakub Mensik.

Formula One. George Russell will start Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix from the back of the grid, after a power unit penalty carried over from last weekend's race.

No Super Rugby or Warriors fixtures today.

Coming up. The Bledisloe Cup test between the All Blacks and Wallabies is at Eden Park on Saturday. The Singapore Grand Prix runs Sunday. Election campaign coverage continues, with ACT and National both due to release fiscal plans this weekend.

End of flash.
